summary.name: CopyQ
summary.one_liner: CopyQ is an open-source clipboard manager with tabbed clipboard history, editing, and scripting features.
use_cases: Keep a searchable history of copied text and images
Organize saved clipboard items into custom tabs
Automate clipboard actions with scripts and the command line
Create system-wide shortcuts for pasting saved items
Edit clipboard contents with a Vim-like editor
summary.what_it_does: CopyQ monitors the system clipboard and saves its content into customized tabs, so saved items can be pasted later into any application. It stores text, HTML, images and other custom formats, and lets you browse, filter, sort, edit, remove, and drag-and-drop items. Items can have notes or tags added. It supports system-wide shortcuts with custom commands, a command-line interface and scripting, and ignoring clipboard content copied from certain windows or containing certain text. Items are restored when the app restarts.
notable: Command-line interface and scripting, with the main app required to be running
Tabbed clipboard history with notes and tags on items
Install via installer, portable zip, Scoop, Chocolatey, Homebrew, PPA, Flatpak, or build from source
caveats: Command-line commands only work while the main CopyQ application is running
Source build instructions list Qt5-based dependencies, and the page does not state a current Qt version
The page lists OS X 10.15+ as the macOS requirement
